rules_evaluated.evidence: L3-7 slide 1 body (expanded view): "the team ships them before any customer can say a guess was wrong" is the nearest to flattening the Day 2 unease, and it stays inside: it names the not-knowing (no customer evidence) and hands a concrete first move (book interviews), without resolving to the relief the next lecture 'Widen before you choose' owns. Student leaves: uncertain whether their bets rest on customer facts, aware the next move is customer contact; sets up widening. Strategy doc L87: 'Day 2 is that unease.' Teaching beats, mood-floor not at issue.

Slide 1 body: "With no fresh evidence from customers, that something is the team's guesses." Closest to punitive; it blames the missing input, not the student, and 'So a team that does not talk with its customers every week should start there' is a start-point, not a verdict on what they did. Harm (shame) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 '# Go back to your customers' and slide 3 'What customers did beats what they say they will do' lead with the discipline. Closest: slide 1 title 'Without customer contact, agents build your guesses faster' (failure-clause title), but the lecture title is the discipline, the body turns to 'Book the interviews, sit in on support calls', and no failure word (fabrication, hallucination, violation) is used; failure is the negative case the discipline addresses.
